en.greeting: Hi! Today we'll talk about who things belong to, and learn me, him, her, us and them. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Rina's phone
steps.text: In Indonesian you say 'HP Rina'. English turns it around.
steps.body: To show the owner, put the **owner first**, add **'s**, then the thing: **Rina's phone**. Not 'phone Rina' and not 'Rina phone'. It works with any person: **my mother's name**, **Pak Hadi's office**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dewi can't find her phone. You can see it. Which sentence is right?

options: Phone Dewi is on the table.
Dewi's phone is on the table.
Dewi phone's is on the table.
question.explanation: The owner comes first, then **'s**, then the thing: **Dewi's phone**. 'Phone Dewi' is Indonesian word order, and the 's goes on the owner, not on the thing.

steps.title: me, him, her, us, them
steps.text: Now, people after a verb. Indonesian uses 'dia' or '-nya' here; English changes the word.
steps.body: Before the verb: **I, he, she, we, they**. **After** a verb, or after small words like **with, for, to**: **me, him, her, us, them**. So Sari loves Budi → **Sari loves him**, not 'Sari loves he'. **you** and **it** don't change. No 'to' after call or help: **Call me**, not 'Call to me'.

steps.title: In real sentences
steps.text: Look at the word right after the verb or after with.
steps.body: In each sentence the object pronoun comes after the verb or after **with**: **her, us, me, it, them**.

examples.en: Rina is my best friend. I call her every day.
examples.id: Rina sahabat saya. Saya meneleponnya setiap hari.
Pak Hadi mengajari kami bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: This coffee is good. I like it.
My shoes are old. I don't like them.
examples.id: Sepatu saya sudah tua. Saya tidak suka.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think: is the missing word before or after the verb?

question.prompt: Andi is in my class. I sit next to ___.
question.explanation: The word comes after **next to**, so we need the object pronoun. Andi is a man: **he → him**. **his** is for things he owns (his bag).

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Your friends from the office eat with you every day. Say it in English.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kami makan siang bersama mereka.
question.explanation: **We** is the subject, before the verb. After **with** we need the object pronoun: **they → them**. So: **We have lunch with them.**

steps.title: Whose …?
steps.text: What if you don't know the owner? Ask with **Whose**.
steps.body: Ask **Whose + thing + is this?** Answer with 's: **It's Andi's.** or **It's Andi's pen.** You can also say **It's my pen.** Careful: **whose** sounds like **who's**, but **who's** = **who is**.

steps.title: Ask about the owner
steps.text: You find a phone on your desk at the office. It isn't yours.

question.explanation: We ask about the owner, so **whose**, and the thing comes right after it: **Whose phone is this?** 'Who's' means 'who is', and 'Whose is phone this' has the words in the wrong order.

steps.title: Answer the question
steps.text: Your friend shows you a helmet and asks you. Choose the right answer.

question.prompt: Whose helmet is this? (Helm ini punya Sari.)
question.explanation: To answer Whose, use the owner + **'s**: **It's Sari's.** 'It's Sari' means the helmet is Sari herself, and 'of Sari' isn't used for people's things.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards to remember the forms.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for later.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kita belajar cara bilang milik siapa sebuah benda, dan berkenalan dengan me, him, her, us dan them. Pelan-pelan saja, ya.

steps.title: Rina's phone
steps.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bilang 'HP Rina'. Bahasa Inggris membaliknya.
steps.body: Untuk menunjukkan pemilik, letakkan **pemiliknya dulu**, tambahkan **'s**, lalu bendanya: **Rina's phone**. Bukan 'phone Rina' dan bukan 'Rina phone'. Ini berlaku untuk siapa saja: **my mother's name**, **Pak Hadi's office**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dewi tidak menemukan HP-nya. Kamu melihatnya. Kalimat mana yang benar?

options: Phone Dewi is on the table.
Dewi's phone is on the table.
Dewi phone's is on the table.
question.explanation: Pemilik ditulis dulu, lalu **'s**, lalu bendanya: **Dewi's phone**. 'Phone Dewi' adalah urutan bahasa Indonesia, dan 's ditempel pada pemiliknya, bukan pada bendanya.

steps.title: me, him, her, us, them
steps.text: Sekarang, orang yang ada setelah kata kerja. Bahasa Indonesia memakai 'dia' atau '-nya'; bahasa Inggris mengganti katanya.
steps.body: Sebelum kata kerja: **I, he, she, we, they**. **Setelah** kata kerja, atau setelah kata kecil seperti **with, for, to**: **me, him, her, us, them**. Jadi Sari loves Budi → **Sari loves him**, bukan 'Sari loves he'. **you** dan **it** tidak berubah. Tidak ada 'to' setelah call atau help: **Call me**, bukan 'Call to me'.

steps.title: Dalam kalimat nyata
steps.text: Perhatikan kata tepat setelah kata kerja atau setelah with.
steps.body: Di setiap kalimat, object pronoun ada setelah kata kerja atau setelah **with**: **her, us, me, it, them**.

examples.en: Rina is my best friend. I call her every day.
examples.id: Rina sahabat saya. Saya meneleponnya setiap hari.
Pak Hadi mengajari kami bahasa Inggris.

examples.en: This coffee is good. I like it.
My shoes are old. I don't like them.
examples.id: Sepatu saya sudah tua. Saya tidak suka.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pikirkan: kata yang hilang ada sebelum atau sesudah kata kerja?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Andi is in my class. I sit next to ___.
question.explanation: Katanya ada setelah **next to**, jadi kita butuh object pronoun. Andi laki-laki: **he → him**. **his** untuk benda miliknya (his bag).

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Teman-teman kantormu makan bersamamu setiap hari. Katakan dalam bahasa Inggris.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kami makan siang bersama mereka.
question.explanation: **We** adalah subjek, sebelum kata kerja. Setelah **with** kita butuh object pronoun: **they → them**. Jadi: **We have lunch with them.**

steps.title: Whose …?
steps.text: Bagaimana kalau kamu tidak tahu pemiliknya? Tanyakan dengan **Whose**.
steps.body: Tanyakan **Whose + benda + is this?** Jawab dengan 's: **It's Andi's.** atau **It's Andi's pen.** Kamu juga bisa bilang **It's my pen.** Hati-hati: **whose** bunyinya seperti **who's**, tapi **who's** = **who is**.

steps.title: Tanyakan pemiliknya
steps.text: Kamu menemukan HP di mejamu di kantor. Itu bukan HP-mu.

question.explanation: Kita menanyakan pemiliknya, jadi **whose**, dan bendanya langsung setelahnya: **Whose phone is this?** 'Who's' artinya 'who is', dan 'Whose is phone this' urutannya salah.

steps.title: Jawab pertanyaannya
steps.text: Temanmu menunjukkan sebuah helm. Pilih jawaban yang benar.

question.prompt: Whose helmet is this? (Helm ini punya Sari.)
question.explanation: Untuk menjawab Whose, pakai pemilik + **'s**: **It's Sari's.** 'It's Sari' artinya helmnya adalah Sari sendiri, dan 'of Sari' tidak dipakai untuk barang milik orang.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartunya supaya bentuknya makin nempel.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti, ya.
